title: Breakfast Poutine
subtitle: Crispy fries under peppery gravy, cheese curds, and fried eggs.
description: Crispy fries, rich gravy, cheese curds, and a fried egg on top. Canadian firehall comfort that hits after an overnight.

ingredients.name: cheese curds
ingredients.notes: or cubed mozzarella if curds unavailable

ingredients.name: green onions
ingredients.notes: sliced, and hot sauce at the line

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Breakfast Poutine in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Crisp the fries
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Spread fries on sheet pans in a single layer with oil and salt. Roast until deeply golden and crisp—soft fries kill poutine.

steps.title: Make sausage gravy
steps.instruction: Brown sausage, sprinkle flour over the fat, and cook 1 minute. Whisk in milk gradually, simmer until thick enough to coat a spoon. Season aggressively with black pepper. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.instruction: Fry eggs sunny-side up in batches with crisp edges on the whites. Hold on a warm tray—yolks should stay runny for the full poutine experience.

steps.title: Assemble on trays
steps.instruction: Pile hot fries on hotel pans or plates. Scatter cheese curds, ladle hot gravy to partially melt them, then crown each portion with a fried egg.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Serve immediately
steps.instruction: Finish with green onion and hot sauce at the line. Poutine waits for no one—serve the moment eggs hit the fries. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Roast fries first and hold in a warm oven uncovered so they stay crisp until gravy hits.
Make gravy in a wide skillet so it stays hot and pourable—reheat with a splash of milk if it tightens.
Fry eggs last in sync with gravy ladle—one cook assembles while another keeps the egg pan moving.
cleanupNotes: Degrease sheet pans with hot water and a splash of vinegar before scrubbing starch and oil residue.
Scrape the gravy skillet while warm; flour-milk paste sets like concrete once cooled.
leftovers: Poutine does not reheat well; plan portions tightly and repurpose extra fries into a breakfast hash.
Leftover gravy reheats smoothly with milk over low heat—serve over biscuits the next morning.
